title: Affine lifting of a map from a perfect complex
statement: Let X be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let U be a quasi-compact open, let E' be an object of D_QCoh(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category], and let A be a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-perfect-complex]. For every morphism \alpha:A|_U\to E'|_U, there exist a perfect object A' of D(\mathcal O_X), a morphism \beta:A'\to A that is an isomorphism on U, and a morphism \gamma:A'\to E' such that \alpha=\gamma|_U\circ(\beta|_U)^{-1}; moreover A'=A\otimes^L I for some perfect object I of D(\mathcal O_X), with \beta induced by a morphism I\to\mathcal O_X. In particular, if A is supported on a closed subset T, then A' is supported on T.

proof.text: Since A is perfect and E' lies in D_QCoh(O_X), the object R:=R\mathcal Hom_{O_X}(A,E') lies in D_QCoh(O_X) [lem-sc-rhom-supported-qcoherent] (no boundedness of E' is needed for a perfect source). Its restriction to U is canonically R|_U\cong R\mathcal Hom_{O_U}(A|_U,E'|_U) [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-restrict-open], and applying the global-sections statement [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] to the ringed space (U,O_U) (the site of opens of U) gives H^0(U,R|_U)\cong Hom_{D(O_U)}(A|_U,E'|_U). Let s\in H^0(U,R|_U) be the element corresponding to \alpha.

source.place: Tag 08EH, proof (alpha determines a section of RHom(E,E') over U, via cohomology-lemma-section-RHom-over-U)

proof.text: Since U is quasi-compact and the principal opens form a basis of X, write U=D(f_1)\cup\cdots\cup D(f_r). Apply the representability proposition [lem-sc-affine-perfect-open-represent-cohomology] to E=R, which lies in D_QCoh(O_X) by Step 1: there are e\ge1 and a morphism \xi:I_e\to R whose image in H^0(U,R|_U) is s, i.e. \xi|_U\circ(u_e|_U)^{-1}=s under Hom_{D(O_U)}(O_U,R|_U)=H^0(U,R|_U); moreover I_e is perfect and u_e|_U is an isomorphism.

Put I=I_e, u=u_e and A'=A\otimes^L I; A' is perfect because A and I are [lem-sc-perfect-derived-tensor-perfect]. Let \gamma:A'\to E' correspond to \xi under the derived tensor-Hom adjunction [lem-sc-affine-perfect-derived-tensor-hom], and let \beta=\mathrm{id}_A\otimes u:A'\to A. Restriction to U commutes with \otimes^L and with R\mathcal Hom [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-restrict-open], so \beta|_U=\mathrm{id}\otimes(u|_U) is an isomorphism, and by naturality of the adjunction in I (applied to (u|_U)^{-1}:O_U\to I|_U) the morphism \gamma|_U\circ(\beta|_U)^{-1}:A|_U\to E'|_U corresponds to \xi|_U\circ(u|_U)^{-1}=s, hence equals \alpha by the choice of s in Step 1.

source.place: Tag 08EH, proof (E_1 = Tot(I(f^e) tensor M), maps to E and E')

proof.text: By construction A'=A\otimes^L I with I perfect and \beta induced by u:I\to O_X. If A is supported on a closed subset T, then A|_{X\setminus T}=0, so A'|_{X\setminus T}=A|_{X\setminus T}\otimes^L I|_{X\setminus T}=0 (restriction to an open commutes with \otimes^L), i.e. A' is supported on T.
